title: Human-in-the-loop gates
summary: Which shell commands need a human: irreversible ones, outward-facing ones, project-specific patterns, and whether a host prompts natively or the pre-tool hook hands the command over.

questions.prompt: Which shell commands need a human?

options.label: Irreversible and outward-facing commands
options.tradeoff: Pushes, pull requests, releases and destructive commands always ask; more prompts, and a feature-branch push is not told from a default-branch push; free-commands lets chosen ones (git-push) through.

options.label: Irreversible commands only
options.tradeoff: Force-push, hard reset, rm -rf and destructive SQL ask; pushes and releases go through unprompted.

options.label: Outward-facing commands only
options.tradeoff: Pushes, pull requests, releases and publishing ask; local destructive commands go through unprompted.

options.label: Instruction only
options.tradeoff: No friction; depends on the agent complying.

questions.prompt: Which project commands also need a human? A command prefix or a /regex/.

Which outward-facing commands may run without asking? A catalog id such as git-push (plain pushes; force-push and branch deletion still ask), pr-merge (merging a pull request; opening and closing one still ask) or comment-post. The ids name the action; the hosting provider (GitHub) supplies its commands. The earlier GitHub-named ids (gh-pr, gh-pr-merge and the like) still work.

Which outward commands may an autonomous run or a remembered approval allow without asking? Only these are decided at use, by their preconditions (merge: green checks, the default branch as base, and in a run a pull request tied to a step of the run); the rest keep asking. Tags, releases and publishing can never be listed. Where the host's hook can ask it asks the first time and remembers; elsewhere a person starts a run or runs go-getter approvals allow <id>. An MCP write tool is listed as mcp:<server>:<tool>.
May agents use MCP servers without a project list?

options.label: No project policy
options.tradeoff: The host's own MCP settings decide; go-getter neither allows nor denies a server.

options.label: Only listed servers
options.tradeoff: The pre-tool hook denies a call to any MCP server not on the list, on hosts whose hook shows the server; an empty list allows no MCP at all.

questions.prompt: Which MCP servers may agents use? Write each as the host shows it (letters, digits, _ . -); a server the host renames (spaces and dots become _ on some hosts) is compared after the same renaming. An empty list allows no MCP.
Which MCP tools only read? Write each as server:tool. These run without asking; any other tool of an allowed server is a write and asks once (or is granted by a run).

decisions.title: Gated actions need a human
decisions.body:
## Decision

Irreversible and outward-facing shell commands need a human: native ask rules on hosts that support them, a pre-tool hook hand-over on the others (pack {{pack.id}}@{{pack.version}}).

## Why

Decision 0043 asks agents to stop before costly actions; nothing enforces it without a gate (decision 0094).

guardrails.title: Irreversible and outward-facing commands need a human

frontmatter.derivation-note: Given agents must hand over before irreversible or outward-facing actions (0043), the host must ask a human or deny the command, since an instruction alone fails silently.

enforcement.check: Host ask rules and the pre-tool hook gate these commands

guardrails.body:
## Guardrail

Shell commands of the irreversible and outward-facing classes need a human: do not run them yourself, ask the user to run them or approve them. Hosts with project ask rules prompt natively, because `go-getter apply` writes the rules into their settings. The other hosts get a hand-over: the pre-tool hook denies the command and the human runs it. `go-getter coverage` shows the tier per host. A mode that skips permission prompts defeats the native rules. A wrapped command (`sh -c`, `eval`) is matched on its literal text only.

decisions.title: Irreversible commands need a human
decisions.body:
## Decision

Irreversible shell commands (force-push, history rewrite, hard reset, `rm -rf`, destructive SQL, deleting a branch or tag) need a human: native ask rules on hosts that support them, a pre-tool hook hand-over on the others (pack {{pack.id}}@{{pack.version}}).

## Why

Decision 0043 asks agents to stop before costly actions; nothing enforces it without a gate (decision 0094).

decisions.title: Outward-facing commands need a human
decisions.body:
## Decision

Outward-facing shell commands (push, pull requests, releases, tags, publishing, issue comments) need a human: native ask rules on hosts that support them, a pre-tool hook hand-over on the others (pack {{pack.id}}@{{pack.version}}).

## Why

Decision 0043 asks agents to stop before costly actions; nothing enforces it without a gate (decision 0094).

decisions.title: Gated actions are advisory
decisions.body:
## Decision

Agents are told to hand over before irreversible or outward-facing actions; nothing blocks them (pack {{pack.id}}@{{pack.version}}).

## Why

The project accepted the risk for less friction (decision 0043).

guardrails.title: Agents hand over before irreversible or outward-facing actions

frontmatter.derivation-note: Given the project chose no mechanical gate, the rule rests on the agent following it.

guardrails.body:
## Guardrail

Ask the user before irreversible or outward-facing commands. Advisory (tier 1): nothing blocks them.

decisions.title: Project-specific commands that also need a human are listed
decisions.body:
## Decision

Commands matching the extra patterns [{{answer.extra-patterns}}] also need a human, on top of the gated classes (pack {{pack.id}}@{{pack.version}}); an empty list adds none.

## Why

The catalog cannot know a project's own deploy or release commands, so the project names them (decision 0094).

decisions.title: Outward-facing commands that run without asking are listed
decisions.body:
## Decision

The commands [{{answer.free-commands}}] run without a human, though they are outward-facing (pack {{pack.id}}@{{pack.version}}); an empty list frees none. Irreversible commands and every other outward-facing command still need a human.

## Why

A plain push to a feature branch is reversible, and a push to the default branch is stopped by a git hook or branch protection, so asking for each one adds friction without protection (decision 0120).

decisions.title: Outward commands a run or a remembered approval may allow are listed
decisions.body:
## Decision

The outward commands [{{answer.run-grants}}] may run without a prompt when an autonomous run grants them or a person approved them once, and only while their preconditions hold at that use (pack {{pack.id}}@{{pack.version}}); an empty list grants none. Tags, releases, publishing and history rewrites always need a human.

## Why

Confirming each merge of a plan whose order is fixed is friction without protection when required checks and branch protection already bound the work; the preconditions keep a remembered approval from outliving the conditions that made it safe (decision 0130).

decisions.title: MCP servers agents may use are listed
decisions.body:
## Decision

Agents may use the MCP servers [{{answer.mcp-servers}}]; a call to any other server is denied by the pre-tool hook where the host shows the server in the tool name (pack {{pack.id}}@{{pack.version}}); an empty list allows no MCP.

## Why

An MCP server is third-party code and data an agent calls with the project's context; a list is cheap to state and to audit (decision 0138).

guardrails.title: Agents use only the allowlisted MCP servers

frontmatter.derivation-note: Given an MCP server is third-party code reached with the project's context (0138), a call to a server the project did not list must be refused by the host's hook, since an instruction alone fails silently.

enforcement.check: The pre-tool hook denies a call to an MCP server that is not listed

guardrails.body:
## Guardrail

Use only the MCP servers the project lists. A call to another server is denied by the pre-tool hook on hosts whose hook shows the server name in the tool call; on the others the list is advisory (fact 0036). A tool not marked read is a write: it asks once where the hook can ask and is remembered, or a run grants it; elsewhere a person runs `go-getter approvals allow mcp:<server>:<tool>`. `go-getter coverage` shows the tier per host.

decisions.title: No project list of MCP servers
decisions.body:
## Decision

The project sets no list of MCP servers; the host's own settings decide which servers agents use (pack {{pack.id}}@{{pack.version}}).

## Why

The project accepted the host's defaults for less setup (decision 0138); choosing `allowlist` makes the pre-tool hook deny unlisted servers.

decisions.title: MCP tools that only read run without asking
decisions.body:
## Decision

The MCP tools [{{answer.mcp-read-tools}}] only read and run without a prompt; every other tool of an allowed server is a write and needs a remembered approval or a run grant (pack {{pack.id}}@{{pack.version}}); an empty list marks none.

## Why

Reads stay usable unattended while writes ask once and are remembered, reusing the approvals store and the run record (decision 0138).
